title: Boundaries and 'Not Sure'
goals: Identify a specific source of uncertainty and explain how it affects a prediction
Compare predictions across stated possible inputs without inventing a missing value
Design a review step with relevant evidence and an explicit unresolved outcome
vocabulary: Something relevant that the available evidence does not settle
An input still compatible with the stated information
A stated condition that sends a case for an additional check
Information gathered to investigate the reason a case was referred
Still not settled after the available checks

worked_example.title: Match the review to the cause

rows: Check how the record was made
Check the label policy and sources

blocks.text: A review request should carry the original input, model version, unresolved issue and any predictions already made. Name the evidence to seek and the person responsible for checking it. A reviewer needs access to relevant evidence and a clear task; being human does not make an unsupported guess correct.

After review, record what was checked and what changed. If a reliable new reading establishes 6 cm, the model predicts tall. If the record is still unreadable, keep no prediction with reason unresolved height. Do not replace the original record without retaining the reason for the correction.

guided_practice.title: Keep a stable prediction within its limits
guided_practice.prompt: Assume the only possible heights are 8 and 9 cm. Apply tall at least 6 to each. Write a justified result statement and two things it does not establish. Do not invent a confidence percentage.
guided_practice.answer: Both inputs predict tall, so the prediction is tall under both listed possibilities. This does not identify whether the exact height is 8 or 9 and does not establish agreement with the correct task label. Outside the exercise, completeness of the possibilities also needs evidence.

independent_case.title: Transfer the method to distance
independent_case.task: A paper model predicts far at a distance of at least 4 units, otherwise near, for whole-number distances 1 through 8. For each complete possibility set, compare predictions: 2 or 3; 3 or 4; 4 or 5. Identify the set requiring review before a single category can be stated. Design a relevant check and an unresolved ending. Limit the claims for the other two sets.
independent_case.answer: At 2 or 3 both predict near. At 3 predict near and at 4 far, so that set leaves the category unresolved. At 4 or 5 both predict far. Request a reliable distance reading in the stated units for the disputed set; if unavailable retain no single category and reason unresolved distance. The other two predictions are stable only across their listed possibilities, not verified as correct labels or exact distances.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: Two possible values imply equal probabilities
A list of possibilities supplies no probabilities unless further evidence states them.
Averaging guesses recovers the missing input
A calculated average is a new assumption, not an observed measurement.
Repeated identical outputs remove input uncertainty
Re-running unchanged information does not reveal a missing digit or unit.
A human reviewer can always settle the case
Require relevant evidence and allow an explicit unresolved outcome.

blocks.text: INPUT  features with incomplete or conflicting clues
PROCESS  compare evidence with category boundaries
OUTPUT  category, not sure, or request more information
CORE IDEA  Overlapping categories create uncertainty; abstaining can be responsible.

UNDER THE HOOD  Abstention is a decision policy: when confidence or evidence fails a threshold, the system defers. Good thresholds balance coverage against error cost and specify what additional information or human review follows.

A closer explanation

blocks.title: Possible heights can change the prediction
blocks.caption: A shared prediction across the listed possibilities does not identify the exact input or prove the category correct. Different predictions show that the unknown input can change this model’s result.

blocks.text: At either 5 or 6 cm, one possibility predicts short and the other tall. Record no single category yet and ask for the original record or a new measurement. Do not select the more convenient digit. Averaging the two readings would introduce a different input that neither possibility stated.

At either 8 or 9 cm, the model predicts tall in both cases. You can state that the prediction stays tall under these two possibilities. Keep the exact-height uncertainty visible. This agreement does not check the model against a correct task label or establish that the list of possible heights is complete.
